mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Y-o-y GDPC1 growth accelerates by > 2pp but SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the unemployment rate below 5% signals a tightening labor market that will drive wage inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the Fed tightens policy.
failure_condition: UNRATE drops below 5% but SPX 20-day returns are positive > 60% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production growth slows by more than 2% y-o-y, it signals a supply crunch that will drive inflation and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Y-o-y INDPRO growth slows by > 2pp but SPX 60-day returns are positive > 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 3%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that will slow economic growth and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 3% but SPX 20-day returns are positive > 60% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts growth accelerates by more than 20% y-o-y, it signals overexuberance in the housing market that will lead to a slowdown and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Y-o-y HOUST growth > 20% but SPX 60-day returns are positive > 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment growth slows by more than 100k jobs per month for 3 consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 3mo PAYEMS growth < -100k but SPX 20-day returns are positive > 60% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI inflation rate rises above 3% y-o-y, and the federal funds rate is below 2%, it signals that monetary policy is too loose, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the Fed is forced to tighten.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL y-o-y > 3% and FEDFUNDS < 2% but SPX 60-day returns are positive > 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When real consumer spending growth slows by more than 2% q-o-q, and the unemployment rate is rising, it signals a weakening consumer sector that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS q-o-q growth < -2% and UNRATE rising
failure_condition: RSAFS q-o-q growth < -2% and UNRATE rising but SPX 20-day returns are positive > 60% of the time.
